RunPlan engineering assessment and saved-format decision

Source: vignettes/articles/contributor-tools-components-runplan-decision.Rmd
contributor-tools-components-runplan-decision.Rmd

Contributing · Object model · Discovery walkthrough · Object fields

A validated list was a reasonable implementation: the old constructor, explicit input certificate and consume/commit guards already enforced its important contract. Numerical kernels have no dispatch requirement. S4 is not inherently more correct or immutable, and the representation change has no claimed speed benefit. Retaining the list would have been a defensible smaller change.

The requested small RunPlan class is also a reasonable domain boundary here: its eight stable fields are used across preparation, context construction, execution, result commit and saved provenance. Typed slots and one structural validity function make that contract inspectable beside the other domain objects. This is a modest maintainability benefit, not a reason to turn every nested list into another class. Screen/design/cell/assignment checks still live at contextual boundaries, and kernels still receive ordinary numerical inputs.

There is one authoritative typed payload. run_plan_payload() provides a canonical temporary value for hashing and legacy interoperation; it is not a second persisted, mutable settings store. New plans snapshot data.tables that could otherwise be changed by reference. Ordinary data.frames retain R’s copy-on-modify behavior. Arbitrary slot or reference mutation is not prevented by S4; consume boundaries verify structural validity and the original payload certificate before using a plan.

The outer saved schema remains 3. The coordinator/component meanings and the canonical execution-hash payload remain unchanged; explicit adapters recognize old schema 3 list plans and response-cache layouts. Known old plans, including history, convert without recomputing budgets, pairs or input identities. A real pre-change fixture retains currentness and its original certificate. Malformed or tampered plans are kept as historical evidence and cannot be re-signed during conversion. Schema 1/2 unknown provenance stays historical.

Developed by Timothy Barry, Louis Deutsch, Eugene Katsevich, Wharton Analytics, National Science Foundation.
